minutes.headline: Parks Commission interviewed three project-management firms for the $8.5M park project and ranked Skanska first, NV5 second, Atlantic third.
minutes.summary: The commission heard presentations from three owner's project manager (OPM) candidates (Skanska, Atlantic, NV5) for the park and ball-field project, and asked about ledge, wetlands, a historic underground structure, procurement and change orders. After the last interview the commissioners deliberated and moved a ranked list, which goes to the town manager for fee negotiation. The meeting adjourned at 9:46.

votes.motion: Rank Skanska first, NV5 second and Atlantic third as the OPM list, with the town manager to negotiate a fee, falling back to the next firm if needed.

budget_items.what_was_said: Skanska noted the identified budget for the project and that its first task would be to firm up schedule and budget.
The commission said grants and other sources, including ARPA, have been raised without town tax money, with a water conservation grant as the latest.
The town gave seed money for engineering, ARPA funds served as matching funds, and the state granted money for the park.
The chair said the project's cost rose from the original estimate to the current one without contingency, and that a fall town meeting request is planned for matching funds.
Skanska described reviewing a contractor's mechanical change order for DCAM and estimating it far lower than claimed.
Skanska described ledge costs on a private project growing quickly and said grading to avoid blasting is the aim.
Atlantic argued for splitting site work and modular building procurement to avoid general contractor markup and double bonding.

decisions.decision: The commission will send a ranked list to the town manager, who will negotiate the contract and fee; a result is expected over the next week or so.
Commissioners' stated ranking: Skanska first, NV5 second, Atlantic third, with NV5 as the fallback if a price cannot be negotiated with Skanska.
Atlantic was named the bottom choice by at least two commissioners during deliberation, before the ranking motion.

The ranked list goes to the town manager to negotiate a fee, falling back to the next firm if a price cannot be agreed; a result was expected within about a week.

why_it_matters: The firm chosen will manage a park and ball-field project whose cost has grown, so its fee and its handling of ledge, change orders and procurement bear on how much the town is asked to provide.
Residents may be asked at a fall town meeting to vote on matching funds for the project, which has so far leaned on grants and ARPA money rather than local taxes.
